new_results.statement: If K(r,.) is C0 and K(r,v)<=g(r) for a probability density g in Lp, p>2, then T=R+bV^2 has p_T in C0 and ||p_T||inf <= 2sqrt(2(p-1)/(p-2)) |b|^-1/2 ||g||p^[p/(2(p-1))].
The completed logarithmic envelope implies an explicit Lp ladder for every invertible indefinite physical pair; at p=3, ||p_pair||3 <=4*3^(1/6)|det S|^-1/4 sigma_min(S)^-1/6.

For B=[[C,a],[a^T,b]] with b!=0, a!=0 and indefinite S=C-aa^T/b, the affine three-coordinate output has a C0 density bounded by 8sqrt(2)3^(1/8)|b|^-1/2|det S|^-3/16 sigma_min(S)^-1/8, uniformly over cap-one product laws and affine terms; same under outside conditioning.

Every invertible indefinite physical 3x3 block is paid locally either by account02/B15's collective indefinite-pair/rank-one-Schur theorem or, if no physical pair is indefinite, by the new coupled-pivot/indefinite-Schur theorem.
A generic sup_t P(|R-t|<rho)<=H sqrt(rho) certificate, even with p_R in L1 intersect L2, does not imply bounded density after adding one independent cap-one square.

actual_partner_application: On Q_m=(P1+L1)^2-(P2-L2)^2+m^-1(sum W_j)^2, partner theorem has Delta=kappa=sigma=1 and gives ||p_Qm||inf<=8sqrt(2) uniformly in m. Therefore input L1 distance delta gives output Lr distance <=(16sqrt(2))^(1-1/r)delta^(1/r) for every finite r.
